picks.excerpt: Epic Games has sold ArtStation and Sketchfab to KitBash3D, and game artists are openly celebrating — 'free from Epic and their love of AI slop' — after years of complaints that AI-generated art flooded the portfolio site and 3D marketplace. The handover reopens the question of how the industry's main game-art portfolio platform will police generative AI listings.
picks.rationale: The industry's main game-art portfolio and 3D asset marketplace changes owner, directly resetting the AI-listing policy every game artist publishes under.

picks.excerpt: Twitch streamers discovered their streams, VODs and chat were enrolled in Amazon's AI training by default, and are circulating opt-out instructions plus an 'aioptedout' tag. Twitch's chief product officer conceded the design rationale out loud: 'If it was opt in, nobody would opt in.'
picks.rationale: Anyone streaming their work is opted into Amazon's model training by default — this is the version of the story that carries the opt-out steps and the platform's own admission.

picks.excerpt: At a KRAFTON x ReLU Games dev talk, the Mimesis team laid out an 'AI game design' methodology: AI should generate new play experiences, not just speed up production. They detailed scrapping the failed Doppelgänger prototype, their Nolan platform for rapid AI-assisted prototyping, and why small purpose-trained networks beat LLMs for a player-mimicking NPC.
picks.rationale: A rare concrete design methodology — prototyping platform, a scrapped prototype post-mortem, and small purpose-trained nets over LLMs — rather than another AI-in-games opinion.

picks.excerpt: Dean Takahashi asks how outsourcing and co-development studios — the backbone of AAA art and production pipelines — will actually deploy AI tools for their publisher clients as the ecosystem contracts. The column reframes the AI question from 'will it replace devs' to 'who owns the pipeline when the work is external.'
picks.rationale: Shifts the AI question to the outsourced art and co-dev studios that actually build most AAA assets, and to who owns the pipeline when the work is external.

picks.excerpt: Concept art released for Supergirl appears to carry generative-AI tells, reigniting the argument over AI in big-budget character and creature design. The flashpoint is concept art specifically — the stage of the pipeline studios keep insisting is still human-led.
picks.rationale: The flashpoint is concept art itself — the stage character designers were told stays human-led; flagged for possible cross-section collision with movies.
